newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frost forecast for dormant German winter crops.
newsitem.headline: Frost forecast for dormant German winter crops.

text.p: A cold front with snow and night frosts was in prospect for dormant German winter crops next week, the DWD meteorological institute in Offenbach said in its weekly farm weather report.

A DWD source said a rapidly dropping temperature without snowfall was a theoretical threat to sensitive rapeseed if it had not hardened enough in the autumn, but the crop was mostly in good shape because of a slow start to the winter.
Old crop areas of maize and sugar beet had been fully cleared.
Some 96 percent of the beet crop had been received at factories by Dec 13, the rest was stored alongside fields.
DWD forecast maximum temperatures between minus two and plus two degrees in the period to Tuesday, Dec 24.

This would be followed by snow in the south and temperatures around minus five degrees, accompanied by severe night frosts in eastern Germany, in the period to Dec 26 after DWD measured temperatures of one to six degrees in the period to Dec 18, with south western spikes at 12-15.
